complete_q41_object.question: If Charismatic must Recruit but only one Eyrie warrior remains in supply, can placing that one fulfill the Decree?

complete_q41_object.expected_answer: No. Charismatic requires two; inability fully complete causes immediate turmoil despite maximum-possible piece placement.

answer_key_binding.treatment: The key is a permitted benchmark expectation, independently checked against the Law and FAQ rather than treated as proof of its own correctness.

LAW-1.5.4.description: Prompted piece manipulation must reach the maximum possible; costs and prerequisites remain. Simultaneous removals precede triggered effects. The extraction separates the paragraph continuation because of column layout.

LAW-7.2.1.description: Eyrie craft with roosts before Decree.

LAW-7.5.2.description: Resolve every card, columns left to right, freely order within columns; inability fully to take the action causes immediate Turmoil.

LAW-7.7.description: Any inability fully to take a Decree action triggers Turmoil; its final step ends Daylight.

LAW-7.8.2.description: Charismatic must place two warriors instead of one whenever taking Recruit.

rule_combination_reasoning.reason: The pending Recruit card prompts placement at a legal matching roost; Charismatic changes the required quantity to two. One available warrior cannot supply that full quantity.

The finite-piece and manipulation rules require the maximum possible placement. In this scenario that is one, assuming the ordinary legal roost required by the question. The supplied verified publisher answer directly confirms actual one-warrior placement.

Placing the available one does not transform the two-warrior requirement into a fulfilled Decree. The faction rule still triggers immediate Turmoil because the required action cannot be fully taken. The FAQ supplies no waiver of this requirement.

The actual placement obligation and immediate Turmoil consequence can both be followed, so precedence does not require discarding the general placement rule. Immediate Turmoil bars skipping the failed card or continuing the Decree; it does not itself state that the prompted maximum-possible placement is prohibited.

No extra preflight supply-check rule, optional attempt, partial-attempt prerequisite, trial-and-rollback sequence, or separate timing window is needed or inferred. The publisher answer resolves the placement claim, while the Law resolves fulfillment and Turmoil. Reading immediate as cancelling all placement would conflict with the supplied publisher answer without an express no-placement instruction.

The frozen summary gives the same compatible instructions: maximum possible placement, two required for Charismatic, no waiver of Decree completion, and immediate supply-shortage Turmoil. Both reader responses are supported by their allowed summary.

source_passages.section: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight — resolve the Decree
source_passages.quotation:
| Decree column | Match the card's suit to | Required procedure for one card |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |
| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |
| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there** |

**Bird Decree cards are wild in every column:** choose any clearing suit, while still meeting that action’s other requirements.

If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Piece limits
source_passages.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

answer.ruling: Charismatic must place two warriors for a Decree Recruit. With only one warrior remaining in supply, placing that one does not fully complete the required action; it does not satisfy the Decree card.
